Carlos (Finance): Quick one 12. StreamLeaf billed 21% VAT on sandbox credits to our EU NGO partner (INV-SL-101). Partner says they're VAT-exempt as a registered charity in the Netherlands and provided a Dutch VAT ID. Vendor insists they applied OSS logic. Do we hold refund? cc @Elena Legal @Nadia Tax
TaxBot: Invoice INV-SL-101 uploaded by @StreamLeaf amount: 
31,000VAT: 
36,000 (21%). File: INV-SL-101.pdf
Nadia Tax: High level: OSS is for B2C distance sales of digital services; it doesn't remove VAT where the buyer is a VAT-registered business. For B2B supplies within the EU the reverse charge applies if buyer and seller are both VAT-registered and invoice shows buyer's VAT ID. If buyer is a charity but VAT-registered (has a VAT number) they can be treated as a business for VAT purposes. Need to verify buyer VAT status and whether StreamLeaf has the buyer's VAT on the invoice.
Elena Legal: Also check the place-of-supply rules: SaaS place of supply to a business is the customer location. If buyer is VAT-registered NL entity and has given a valid NL VAT ID, seller should NOT charge NL VAT; invoice should have reverse-charge wording. If buyer is not VAT-registered (even if charity), then seller may need to charge tax under B2C rules or use OSS depending on seller's registration.
Marta (EU Ops): Vendor replied: "We're on OSS in ES and our billing system flagged the customer as non-business and applied Spanish VAT." They attached a screenshot of their billing rule and a copy of the invoice showing NL VAT ID was not present on their billing profile.
Carlos (Finance): Partner provided VAT ID: NL123456789B01 and charity registry extract showing VAT registration. They assert they sent the VAT ID during signup but not on current invoice.
Nadia Tax: Next steps: 1) We need vendor to confirm they did NOT have the buyer VAT ID at invoicing time OR show proof they had it. 2) If they didn't have it, ask for a reissued invoice with reverse-charge text: "Reverse charge 1 VAT to be accounted for by the recipient (Article 196 VAT Directive)." 3) If they used OSS incorrectly (treating a VAT-registered customer as consumer), they must refund VAT. 4) If vendor claims OSS was correct, request evidence of OSS declaration covering that period (OSS quarterly summary) and reconciliation showing this invoice was reported.
Elena Legal: Also request a signed statement from StreamLeaf confirming they will reissue or refund. If they refuse, we escalate payment hold and potential chargeback. Keep procurement on loop if commercial dispute.
Carlos (Finance): Putting INV-SL-101 on hold. SLA to vendor: 4 business days to either (a) reissue invoice with reverse charge and attach proof of not reporting under OSS for this invoice, or (b) refund VAT and send proof of refund.
Marta (EU Ops): I'll send suggested vendor text. Do we want them to include OSS monthly/quarterly summary excerpt?
Nadia Tax: Yes, ask for OSS report excerpt showing invoice ID or date range. Also ask vendor to confirm which VAT number they used as customer identifier at time of billing. If VIES lookup needed I can do it.
TaxBot: Quick VIES check: NL123456789B01 returned as VALID for Netherlands (checked 2024-10-12).
Carlos (Finance): Great. Noting action items: Marta to request reissue/refund + OSS excerpt; Nadia to confirm VIES and log evidence; Elena to draft escalation language if vendor doesn't comply. I'll update refunds tracker and only process credit after corrected invoice or refund proof. Closing when credit posts. :white_check_mark:
